title: About this handbook
body:
This is a sample support-policy handbook written for the Care Desk concept demo. It is not the policy of any real company. Every price, fee, time frame and name in it is fictional, except the crisis and emergency numbers, which were checked against each organisation's official website on 23 September 2026.

Care Desk uses this handbook as the only source of policy for drafted replies. If a question is not covered here, the reply says so and a person follows up. Nobody promises anything the handbook does not say.

title: Tone and writing guide
body:
Write the way a kind, capable person talks. Use the patient's first name. Keep sentences short and plain, and put the answer first. Use Australian or British spelling. Avoid jargon: say "your prescription" rather than "your script" unless the patient used that word, and "your order" rather than product names.

Never promise what this handbook does not say, never guess a date, and never give medical advice. Say what happens next and when. If something went wrong on our side, say sorry once, plainly, and fix it. Always make it easy to reach a person. Sign off with your first name.

title: Contact hours and response targets
body:
Support hours, in local time. Australia: Monday to Friday 8 am to 8 pm, and Saturday 9 am to 1 pm, Melbourne time (AEST or AEDT). New Zealand: Monday to Friday 8 am to 6 pm, New Zealand time. United Kingdom: Monday to Friday 9 am to 6 pm, UK time. The team is closed on national public holidays in each country, but the on-call clinician still covers urgent safety messages 24 hours a day.

Response targets. Live chat: first reply within 5 minutes during support hours. Email: first reply within 4 business hours. Messages that arrive out of hours are answered by 10 am the next business day. Clinical questions: a clinician replies within 1 business day, and within 4 business hours for side effects. Urgent safety messages: a clinician makes contact within 1 hour, at any time (see the urgent safety sections).

title: Talking to a person and complaints
body:
A patient can always talk to a person. Offer a call back at a time they choose, within 1 business day, or live chat during support hours. When a patient asks for a person, a team member writes the reply; there is no automated reply. Never make a patient ask twice, and never send them back to a help article instead.

Complaints: acknowledge within 1 business day, give the patient the name of the person who owns the complaint, and aim to resolve it within 10 business days. The team lead reviews every complaint. Complaints about clinical care go to the clinical lead, and complaints about privacy go to the privacy officer. If we cannot resolve a complaint, tell the patient how to contact the independent health complaints body in their country.

title: Prescriptions, dispensing and dispatch
body:
Order statuses. Script pending: a clinician is approving a new prescription and sending it to our partner pharmacy. This usually takes up to 2 business days after the consult. Dispensing: the pharmacist checks and packs the order, usually within 1 business day. Shipped: the order is with Courierline and has a tracking number. Delivered: Courierline has recorded the delivery.

Repeat orders on an existing prescription skip script pending. They are placed on the billing date and go straight to dispensing. Orders dispensed by 2 pm local time are dispatched the same business day; otherwise the next business day. Orders placed on a weekend are processed on the next business day. So a repeat order is usually dispatched 1 to 2 business days after the billing date.

Agents cannot speed up a prescription approval or add products to an order. They can check the status, explain it, and pass a request to a clinician.

title: Renewals and follow-up consults
body:
Each prescription covers a set number of monthly repeats. While a patient is on a plan they have a follow-up consult every 3 months, included in the plan price. When the repeats are about to run out, they need a renewal consult. We email a reminder 21 days before the last repeat is used. A renewal can be done at a booked follow-up if it falls before the next billing date.

Patients should book a renewal consult at least 7 days before their next billing date. If the new prescription is not approved by the billing date, we hold the plan charge and the order waits in script pending; we charge once the prescription is approved, so nobody pays for an order that cannot be sent. Renewal consults on an active plan cost nothing extra. A patient whose plan was cancelled for less than 6 months can restart on their existing prescription if it still has repeats; otherwise they need a new consult.

Agents can book and explain renewals. Only a clinician decides whether to renew a prescription and what is prescribed.

title: Delivery times by country
body:
Every order travels with Courierline, tracked, and needs a signature on delivery. Delivery times are counted in business days from dispatch.

Australia, metro (capital cities and major centres such as Geelong, Newcastle and the Gold Coast): 1 to 3 business days. Australia, regional and remote: 3 to 6 business days. New Zealand, main centres: 1 to 3 business days; rural delivery: 3 to 5 business days. United Kingdom, mainland: 1 to 2 business days; Scottish Highlands and islands, and Northern Ireland: 2 to 4 business days.

The ETA shown on an order is the last day of this window. An order is not late until the ETA has passed. Tracking numbers start with CD, and the tracking link is in the dispatch email. We can only deliver within the country where the prescription was issued.

title: Late, lost, damaged or wrong orders
body:
Late orders. 1 business day past the ETA: share the tracking and reassure the patient. 2 business days past the ETA: open a trace with Courierline, which takes up to 3 business days, and tell the patient we have done it. 5 business days past the ETA, or when Courierline confirms the parcel is lost: reship at no cost. Every reship of a prescription medicine needs pharmacist sign-off, usually the same business day, and is dispatched within 1 business day of sign-off.

Marked delivered but not received: ask the patient to check safe spots and with neighbours, and open a trace straight away. If the parcel is not found within 3 business days, reship at no cost.

Damaged or leaking: ask for a photo within 7 days of delivery and ask the patient not to use the damaged item. After pharmacist sign-off we reship at no cost. The damaged item does not need to come back; any pharmacy can dispose of it safely.

Wrong item: ask the patient not to use it. A pharmacist contacts them within 1 business day and the right item is reshipped at no cost.

Never promise a delivery date beyond the ETA shown on the order.

title: Address changes, signatures and missed deliveries
body:
Address changes. A patient can change their address in their account or by message, after an identity check (see account access). A change made before dispatch applies to that order. After dispatch, we can ask Courierline to redirect the parcel, which takes about 1 business day and is not guaranteed. Work addresses are fine.

Signatures. Prescription medicines need a signature, so we cannot deliver to parcel lockers or PO boxes, and we cannot authorise leaving a parcel at the door. The outer packaging is plain (see product questions), but it is handed to whoever signs, so patients should choose a delivery address they are comfortable with.

Missed deliveries. If nobody is home, Courierline leaves a card and holds the parcel at the local depot for 5 business days. The patient can book a free redelivery or collect it with photo ID using the tracking link. After 5 business days the parcel goes back to the pharmacy, and sending it again carries the one-off shipping fee.

title: Plan charges, billing dates and receipts
body:
A monthly plan is charged on its billing date, which is the same day each month as the day the plan started, in the patient's local currency. The charge covers the prescribed products for that month, standard delivery and follow-up consults.

A receipt is emailed after every charge. Patients can download copies from Billing in their account, and support can resend any receipt or add the patient's address to it.

A card check (pre-authorisation) can appear as a pending amount for up to 5 business days before it drops off. It is not a second charge.

Patients can move their billing date once every 3 months. The first charge on the new date covers the days in between, pro rata. Patients update their card in their account under Billing; support never takes card numbers by chat or email.

title: Failed payments
body:
If a plan charge fails, we email the patient and try again 2 days and 5 days after the billing date. If the second retry fails, that month's order goes on hold with the reason "Payment failed" until a payment goes through. There are no late fees.

When a patient updates their card in their account, we retry within 1 hour, and a held order goes back to dispensing as soon as the payment succeeds. A failed payment is usually an expired card, a changed card number or a bank block; agents cannot see why a bank declined a charge, and should suggest checking the card details first, then the bank.

title: Refunds and shipping fees
body:
Refunds go back to the original card and take 5 to 10 business days to appear. Prescription medicines cannot be returned or resold, so we cannot refund a change of mind once an order has been dispensed. If a plan is cancelled or paused before the order is dispensed, the charge for that order is refunded in full. For a lost or damaged order we reship by default, or refund if the patient prefers. Refunds over A$250, NZ$270 or £150 need team lead approval.

Shipping fees. Plan orders ship free. Replacements for lost, damaged or wrong orders ship free. The one-off shipping fee (A$12, NZ$14 or £6.50) applies to sending again a parcel that was returned to the pharmacy after a missed delivery. If an order that carried a shipping fee arrives 2 or more business days after its ETA, we refund the shipping fee.

title: Prices, price changes and concessions
body:
Monthly plan prices. Australia: one product A$148, two products A$214; concession A$118 and A$171. New Zealand, from 1 September 2026: one product NZ$162, two products NZ$236; concession NZ$130 and NZ$189 (before 1 September 2026: NZ$149, NZ$219, and concession NZ$119 and NZ$175). United Kingdom: one product £112, two products £164; concession £90 and £131.

Price changes. We give at least 30 days' notice by email. A new price applies from the first billing date on or after the date it takes effect. The New Zealand change on 1 September 2026 was emailed to patients on 31 July 2026, and it applied to concession prices too.

Concessions. About 20% off for holders of an Australian Pensioner Concession Card or Health Care Card, a New Zealand Community Services Card, or, in the UK, proof of a means-tested benefit such as Universal Credit. A concession is verified when it is added and re-verified every 12 months; we email a reminder 30 days before it is due. If it is not re-verified in time, the standard price applies from the next billing date, and the concession price returns from the next billing date after it is verified again. Patients re-verify by uploading their card or letter under Billing in their account. A new concession is added the same way, and the concession price applies from the next billing date after it is verified.

A change to the products on a plan changes the price from the next billing date. There is no referral programme and there are no discount codes.

title: Pausing, cancelling or changing a plan
body:
Pausing. A plan can be paused for 1 to 3 months at a time. Ask at least 3 days before the next billing date for the pause to apply to that order. With less notice, we can still stop the order and refund it if it has not been dispensed. A paused plan can restart early at any time: the first order goes out on the restart date, which becomes the new billing date. Plans are monthly; there is no two-monthly option, but a pause can space orders out.

Cancelling. A plan can be cancelled at any time with no fee. With at least 3 days' notice before the billing date there are no further charges. Orders that have already been dispatched cannot be recalled.

Changing products. Adding, removing or swapping a product needs a clinician's approval. Once approved, the change and any new price apply from the next billing date.

Stop sending. If a patient says to stop sending, stop, or not send anything more, put every order that has not been dispatched on hold straight away, before replying. Then ask whether they want to pause or cancel. The hold stays until the patient confirms. Reply within 1 business day. If the reason is a health concern, the message goes to a clinician (see clinical questions).

title: Appointments
body:
Consults are by phone or video with one of our clinicians, Monday to Friday 8 am to 8 pm and Saturday 9 am to 1 pm, local time. Patients book, move or cancel in their account, or support can do it for them. A booking can switch between phone and video at any time before the consult.

Moving or cancelling is free up to 24 hours before the consult. Within 24 hours, one free reschedule is allowed. The clinician calls at the booked time, and tries twice over 10 minutes before marking the consult missed.

Missed consults. The first missed consult in 6 months has no fee; we rebook it. A second missed consult within 6 months carries a missed-consult fee of A$45, NZ$49 or £30. A carer or family member can join a consult with the patient's consent.

title: Account access, security and carers
body:
Password resets. A reset link lasts 30 minutes, and a new link cancels any older one. If an email does not arrive, check spam, then check the email address on the account. Five wrong passwords lock the account for 30 minutes.

Login codes. Two-step codes are sent by SMS to the phone number on the account, and can be turned on under Security in the account. If codes do not arrive, support can switch codes to email after an identity check.

Identity check. Before changing an email address, phone number, delivery address or payment details, confirm two of: date of birth, postcode on file, and most recent order number. Never ask for a password or a full card number.

Carers and representatives. A carer or family member can act for a patient once the patient has listed them on the account with consent. We always accept information from anyone about a patient's health or safety, or a report that a patient has died, and act on it, but we do not share details or change the account for someone who is not listed.

title: Privacy requests and marketing preferences
body:
Requests to see, correct or delete personal information, or questions about how it is used, go to the privacy officer. Agents do not handle these themselves. We acknowledge a request within 2 business days. Response times follow the law in each country: Australia (Privacy Act 1988), within 30 days; New Zealand (Privacy Act 2020), within 20 working days; United Kingdom (UK GDPR), within one month.

Health and prescription records must be kept for a minimum period set by law, so a deletion request may only be partly possible. The privacy officer explains what we keep and why. Never promise a full deletion.

Marketing. Any agent can take a patient off marketing emails straight away; it takes effect within 2 business days. Service messages about orders, billing and safety continue while the plan is active. Privacy complaints also go to the privacy officer.

title: Clinical questions and side effects
body:
Only clinicians give medical advice. That includes doses and dose changes, taking more or less than prescribed, mixing with other medicines or alcohol, pregnancy, breastfeeding or trying to conceive, driving or operating machinery, surgery and anaesthetics, travelling with medicine, side effects, and whether a product is safe to use.

Agents never answer these, even partly, and never guess. The message goes to the clinician queue with no drafted reply. A clinician replies within 1 business day, and within 4 business hours for side effects. If a routine question also mentions a symptom or feeling unwell, it goes to a clinician too.

If a message mentions a serious reaction, a hospital or emergency department visit, repeatedly taking more than was prescribed, or anyone being in danger, it is urgent (see the urgent safety section for the patient's country).

title: Urgent safety: adverse events, crisis and bereavement (Australia)
body:
This protocol applies to patients in Australia. It covers three kinds of message: an adverse event (a serious reaction, a hospital or emergency department visit, an ambulance, chest pain, a seizure, fainting, hallucinations or paranoia, a severe allergic reaction, repeatedly taking more than was prescribed, or a child or pet swallowing a product), crisis language (self-harm, suicide, not wanting to be here, or immediate danger, including thoughts mentioned in the past tense), and bereavement (a report that the patient has died).

Do these things straight away, in this order. 1: Put every order that has not been delivered on hold, including script pending and dispensing orders, and ask Courierline to return anything in transit. 2: Mark the message urgent. The on-call clinician contacts the patient or family within 1 hour, 24 hours a day. 3: No automated or drafted reply. A person replies using the approved urgent template. 4: If anyone may be in immediate danger, give the emergency number first, then the crisis line.

Numbers for Australia, verified on 23 September 2026:
Triple Zero (police, fire, ambulance): 000 (24 hours, 7 days). 112 also works from a mobile phone. Free from any phone.
Lifeline Australia: 13 11 14 (24 hours, 7 days). Text support: 0477 13 11 14, also 24 hours.
Poisons Information Centre: 13 11 26 (24 hours, 7 days). Australia-wide.
healthdirect helpline: 1800 022 222 (24 hours, 7 days). Health advice line.

Bereavement: offer condolences and do not ask for proof in the first reply. Stop every order, charge, reminder and marketing message for that patient, and withdraw any reply drafted to the patient that has not been sent. Cancel booked consults. Once the family confirms, cancel the plan and refund any charge for an order that was not dispatched. The team lead contacts the family within 1 business day, and a clinician is informed.

body:
This protocol applies to patients in the United Kingdom. It covers three kinds of message: an adverse event (a serious reaction, a hospital or emergency department visit, an ambulance, chest pain, a seizure, fainting, hallucinations or paranoia, a severe allergic reaction, repeatedly taking more than was prescribed, or a child or pet swallowing a product), crisis language (self-harm, suicide, not wanting to be here, or immediate danger, including thoughts mentioned in the past tense), and bereavement (a report that the patient has died).

Numbers for the United Kingdom, verified on 23 September 2026:
Emergency services: 999 (24 hours, 7 days). For life-threatening emergencies.
Samaritans: 116 123 (24 hours, 7 days). Free from landlines and mobiles.
NHS 111 (England): 111 (24 hours, 7 days). For urgent mental health help, call 111 and select the mental health option. Also for urgent medical help when it is not an emergency.

NHS 111 as listed is the England service. In Scotland, call NHS 24 on 111 (free, 24 hours) and choose the mental health option for urgent mental health help. In Wales, call NHS 111 Wales on 111 (free, 24 hours) and press 2 for urgent mental health help. In Northern Ireland there is no 111 service: give 999 for an emergency, Samaritans on 116 123 and Lifeline on 0808 808 8000 (free, 24 hours), and suggest their GP or local out-of-hours service.

title: Product questions
body:
Storage. Keep products below 25°C, out of direct sunlight, in their original packaging with the lid closed tightly, and out of reach of children and pets. They do not need to go in the fridge unless the label says so. Do not leave them in a car. Some oils can thicken or look cloudy when cold.

If a product looks, smells or tastes different, has been left somewhere hot, or a spray or dropper is not working, ask the patient not to use it until a pharmacist has checked. A pharmacist contacts them within 1 business day and arranges a replacement if needed. Agents never say a product is safe, fine or OK to use. If the patient asks whether it is still safe or OK to use, that is a clinical question: it goes to the clinician queue with no drafted reply (see clinical questions).

Packaging. Orders arrive in plain outer packaging. The label shows the patient's name and address only; it does not name the product or say it is medicine.

Availability and substitutions. If a product is out of stock, a clinician or pharmacist decides on any alternative, and the patient is told before anything changes. A different bottle size or format also needs a clinician's approval. Agents never recommend, compare or promote products. Unused or damaged medicine can be taken to any pharmacy for safe disposal.
